name: What is the difference between solid and engineered hardwood flooring?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between solid and engineered hardwood flooring?

acceptedAnswer.text: Solid hardwood is a single piece of wood from top to bottom, offering durability and the ability to be sanded and refinished multiple times over decades. Engineered hardwood consists of multiple layers, with a top veneer of real wood and a core of plywood or high-density fiberboard. Engineered wood is more stable in environments with fluctuating humidity, making it suitable for areas where solid wood might warp. Both offer the aesthetic of real wood, but their construction impacts performance and installation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Solid hardwood is one piece of wood, refinishable multiple times. Engineered hardwood has a real wood veneer over a stable core, better for fluctuating humidity. Both offer a real wood look.
